Reetech International Ltd is profoundly mispriced by the market because its extreme asset discount completely obscures an explosive inflection in earnings profitability [E2, E15]. The stock trades at a deeply distressed price-to-book ratio of 0.51x against a book value of ₹ 35.6, while the data provider records an even cheaper P/B of 0.49x compared to a sector benchmark of 1.86x [E2, E7]. This asset-heavy cushion of safety is now compounding against a backdrop of fundamental operational revival, highlighted by a massive 176% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E15]. This sudden acceleration in earnings growth has dramatically outpaced 1-year price growth by 226%, showing that the company is starting to outperform expectations as profits surge far beyond the stagnant share price sitting at its 52-week low [E5, E46, E57]. Conceded: [E4, E6, E8, E13, E14, E60].

The bull relies heavily on a low price-to-book ratio of 0.51x and 0.49x to claim a margin of safety [E2, E7], but this asset cushion is rendered meaningless by a dismal return on equity of 1.28% compared to the sector benchmark of 11.49% [E8]. While the bull points to a trailing twelve-month profit growth of 176% [E15] and accelerating earnings [E57], this short-term bounce completely masks a severe multi-year structural decline featuring a 3-year compounded profit growth of -38% and a 5-year contraction of -14% [E13, E14]. Furthermore, the claim of operational revival collapses against the reality of a complete revenue wipeout shown by sales dropping -100% year-over-year [E60]. Conceded: [E2, E7, E15, E46, E57]. The bull's insistence on a cheap valuation ignores that the stock trades at an inflated P/E of 38.04x to 40x against a sector benchmark of just 15.7x [E1, E6], while sitting lifeless at the absolute bottom of its 52-week range with a 0.00% dividend yield [E4, E5].
